judgments.reason: The passage bars zoning from prohibiting duplexes or multi-family housing up to 5 units as of right on residentially zoned lots served by a municipal or centrally managed water and sewer system, which the claim restates in plain terms.

The passage requires as-of-right multifamily or mixed-use at a minimum of 15 units per acre with no minimum parking within 0.5 miles of commuter rail, subway, ferry, or bus stations, matching the claim.
The passage allows up to 3 dwelling units as of right (i.e., without a special permit) on residential lots not connected to municipal or centrally managed water and sewer.
The passage prohibits zoning from barring accessory dwelling units as of right where the principal dwelling contains more than one unit, as the claim states.
The passage bars special permit or discretionary approval requirements for multi-family housing on religious-owned land and requires 20 percent affordable units, matching the claim.
The passage permits reasonable site plan review and setback, bulk, and height regulations while barring height limits below 3 stories, as the claim describes.
The passage allows short-term rental restrictions and prohibitions while barring regulations that individually or cumulatively render such development infeasible.
The passage states no zoning ordinance or by-law shall impose a minimum lot size on new residential developments.
The passage bars parking minimums within .5 miles of commuter rail, ferry, or bus stations and caps requirements at 1 space per unit beyond that distance, exactly as claimed.
The passage directs the board to approve a plan meeting by-right subdivision criteria without a public hearing.
The passage provides that failure to act (or notify) within 21 days results in approval as a by-right subdivision.
The passage bars municipalities from enforcing ordinances restricting primarily residential construction that exceed the section's or DEP's requirements.
The passage states regulations on minimum requirements for subsurface sewage disposal may not exceed the state environmental code for residential housing development.
The passage sets the 15 percent at or below 80 percent AMI or 10 percent at or below 50 percent AMI set-aside for developments of 10 or more units permitted under the cited subsections.
The passage requires each municipality to submit a housing production plan addressing its affordable housing needs to the state every 5 years.
The passage gives municipalities 2 years from receiving an approved housing production plan to adopt or update zoning to comply.

The passage requires the capital asset management commissioner with the housing secretary to determine, before disposition, whether state property should be made available for low or moderate income housing.
The passage voids noncompliant local regulations if a municipality has not conformed by January 1, 2028, as the claim states.
As-of-right permission for duplexes or up to 5 units on sewered residential lots means owners could build without a special permit.
The passage reserves set-aside units for households at or below 80 percent or 50 percent of area median income in developments of 10 or more units.
The passage's as-of-right allowance for duplexes or up to 5 units on residentially zoned, sewered lots matches the claim's personal framing.
The passage prohibits minimum lot size requirements for new residential developments.
The described effect follows from the as-of-right allowance, and the closing consequence stays hedged without adding new facts.
Renters, tenants, leases, and rent levels are each covered by the searched terms that returned no results.
The passage requires as-of-right 15-unit-per-acre multifamily with no parking minimums near rail, subway, ferry, and bus stations, and the added consequence is hedged.
Fares, schedules, and the MBTA each correspond to searched words that do not appear.
Barring minimum parking requirements near commuter rail, ferry, and bus stations directly allows new homes to be built with no parking spaces.
Street parking and parking permits are both covered by the searched terms that returned no results.
The passage states Section 4 takes effect one year after the act's effective date.
The passage provides that noncompliant existing local regulations become null and void if the municipality has not conformed by the stated date.
